thread.title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: Apple's Romp To $1 Trillion Market Cap Helps S&P 500, Nasdaq Notch Gains

author: morningstar.com
title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: Apple's Romp To $1 Trillion Market Cap Helps S&P 500, Nasdaq Notch Gains
text:
By Mark DeCambre, MarketWatch , Ryan Vlastelica
Apple has gained more than $80 billion in value over the past two sessions
U.S. stocks ended a rocky session decidedly higher on the back of a record rally by Apple that took the iPhone maker to a market cap above $1 trillion, a runup that helped Wall Street set aside nettlesome trade issues between the U.S. and China.
What are the benchmarks doing?
The S&P 500 rose 13.86 points to 2,827.22, a gain of 0.5%.
Seven of the 11 primary S&P 500 sectors were in positive territory, with technology leading the advance with a 1.4% gain. Consumer staples rose 1.1%. Meanwhile, materials and energy shares led the decliners, off 0.7% and 0.5%, respectively.
The Nasdaq Composite Index rose 95.40 points, or 1.2%, to 7,802.69, on the back of Apple's advance.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average , however, struggled to hold gains, and closed off 7.66 points, or less than 0.1%, to 25,326.16. Declines in shares of DowDuPont Inc.(DWDP), Goldman Sachs Group Inc. (GS) and McDonald's Corp. (MCD) weighed on the blue-chip benchmark, offsetting Apple's rise.
What's driving markets?
Apple Inc.(AAPL) rose 3% to hit a record price of $207.05, which, if it were to close at that level, would leave it with a market cap of $1 trillion (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/apple-crosses-threshold-needed-for-1-trillion-market-cap-2018-08-02), a first for a publicly traded U.S. company.
Earlier gains had been capped as worries about tensions between Washington and Beijing washed onto Asian shores, hitting major benchmarks in Asia and Europe.
On Wednesday, the Trump administration threatened to more than double proposed tariffs (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/trump-seeks-25-tariffs-on-200-billion-of-goods-imported-from-china-2018-08-01) on $200 billion of Chinese goods to 25%, up from an original 10%. The administration didn't provide specific reasons for such an increase, but the potential for an intensification has helped to unsettle markets during what is typically considered an unfavorable month for stock-market gains (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/after-a-strong-july-august-looks-ominous-for-stocks-2018-07-30).
One of China's premier equity benchmarks, the Shanghai Composite Index , fell 2% on the day and has dropped 21% since a recent peak in January.
Don't miss:Bull market in stocks could be in 'last innings' as bears set sights on strongest sectors (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/bull-market-in-stocks-could-be-in-last-innings-as-bears-set-sights-on-strongest-sectors-2018-08-02)
What else is on investors' radar?
Initial jobless claims rose by 1,000 in the latest week, however they rose less than expected and were near their lowest levels since the 1970s (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/jobless-claims-cling-near-45-year-low-2018-08-02). The report comes a day ahead of the highly anticipated July jobs report. Separately, factory orders rose 0.7% in June.
Investors also digested the latest moves from the Bank of England, which raised its main interest rate (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/bank-of-england-raises-key-lending-rate-to-075-2018-08-02) by 25 basis points to 0.75%, as had been expected.
What are market participants saying
"This market is like living with a volatile family member. If we wake up and trade tensions are bad, then we're down that day. If they're not, then we go up. This is still an amazingly strong market, with an earnings season that has been pretty darn good, but it's difficult for us to rise when you continually hear how bad things are," said JJ Kinahan, chief market strategist at TD Ameritrade.
"Who knows if the latest development changes anything that significantly, but tariffs could certainly stall the momentum in economic growth, and we don't know what the timeline is for this issue to be resolved," he said.
Michael Zezas, a strategist at Morgan Stanley, wrote that "the duration of these conflicts should now be measured in quarters, not weeks."
In a note to clients, he added, "Benign, negotiated outcomes may still be the endgame, but an extended cycle of escalation will allow the conflicts to play out in company financial statements and economic data. it doesn't have to be a material economic problem to be a market negative."
What stocks are in focus
Investors continued to digest results from the second-quarter earnings season, which have mostly supported markets. According to data from JPMorgan, with more than 60% of the market having reported, 86% of companies in the S&P 500 have topped profit expectations, the highest such ratio in its data, which goes back to 2009. Nearly 75% of companies have beaten revenue expectations.
Tesla Inc.(TSLA) jumped 16% a day after the electric-car maker reported quarter revenue that was stronger than expected (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/tesla-stock-rises-after-car-maker-reports-wider-quarterly-loss-but-beats-on-revenue-2018-08-01). The company, shares of which have been extremely volatile throughout 2018, also said it expects to be profitable and cash-flow positive in the second half of the year.
DowDuPont shares ended down 2.2% lower even after the agriculture, materials science and specialty products company beat second-quarter earnings (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/dowduponts-stock-the-lone-dow-gainer-after-earnings-and-revenue-beat-upbeat-outlook-2018-08-02) and revenue expectations and provided an upbeat outlook. Net income was $1.77 billion, or 76 cents a share, compared with $1.32 billion, or $1.07 a share.
Yum Brands Inc.(YUM) posted adjusted second-quarter earnings that beat expectations (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/taco-bell-parent-yum-brands-exceeds-earnings-expectations-2018-08-02), and while revenue fell from the prior year, it was also ahead of forecasts. Shares rose 1.5%.
Teva Pharmaceutical Industries Ltd. (TEVA) tumbled 9.5%. The company reported second-quarter earnings that beat expectations and revenue that was in line with analyst forecasts (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/teva-stock-drops-45-in-spite-of-q2-profit-beat-revenue-match-2018-08-02).
TripAdvisor Inc.(TRIP) tumbled 11.2% after it reported revenue that came in below expectations (http://www.marketwatch.com/discover).
Royal Caribbean Cruises Ltd. (RCL) reported adjusted second-quarter earnings that beat expectations but revenue that was slightly below forecasts (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/royal-caribbean-stock-drops-2-on-q2-revenue-miss-2018-08-02). Shares rose 4%.
Square Inc.(SQ) rose 8.7% after it gave a third-quarter earnings outlook that was below expectations (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/square-stock-choppy-after-results-beat-but-earnings-outlook-falls-short-2018-08-01).
Blue Apron Holdings Inc.(APRN) reported a second-quarter loss that narrowed from the previous year (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/blue-apron-loss-widens-as-revenue-falls-25-2018-08-02) and revenue that fell 25%. The stock plunged 24%, bringing its year-to-date decline to 51%.
MGM Resorts International(MGM) sank 1.6% after it reported second-quarter earnings that missed expectations, along with revenue that was below forecasts (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/mgm-shares-fall-5-in-pre-market-trade-after-earnings-and-revenue-miss-2018-08-02).
Red Robin Gourmet Burgers (RRGB) tumbled 19.3% a day after it gave a weak preliminary second-quarter report (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/red-robin-gourmet-burgers-shares-plummet-24-after-weak-preliminary-earnings-report-2018-08-02).
Cisco Systems Inc.(CSCO) has agreed to buy (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/cisco-dances-with-duo-promises-235b-for-security-startup-2018-08-02) security startup Duo Security for $2.35 billion. Shares of Cisco rose 1.6%.
What other markets are doing
Oil futures (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/oil-prices-deepen-losses-after-surprise-build-in-us-inventories-2018-08-02) reversed earlier losses to rise 1.9% and settle at $68.96 after data reportedly showing a dip in stockpiles. Meanwhile gold futures (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/gold-falls-as-the-dollar-gains-footing-higher-amid-fresh-trade-war-fears-2018-08-02) fell 0.6%, to end at $1,220.10 an ounce, the lowest price in more than a year.
The U.S. dollar index (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/boe-rate-hike-not-enough-to-lift-british-pound-versus-dollar-2018-08-02) strengthened 0.5% to 94.127. European stocks (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/dax-drops-sharply-as-trade-worries-hit-european-stocks-2018-08-02) ended lower for the second session, after Asian markets finished with losses.
--Anora Gaudiano contributed to this article
